points.text: 1 (ventricles) pump / AW, blood a greater distance / into the pulmonary and systemic circulations ;
points.guidance: A to the lungs and to the body; R left into lungs and right to body

points.text: 2 ventricles have more (cardiac) muscle to, pump / AW, blood, at high(er) pressure / with more force (than atria) ;
points.guidance: R if smooth or striated/skeletal muscle; I ‘pump harder’

points.text: 3 (ventricles) pump / AW, blood to overcome a high(er) resistance ;
I answers that only explain why the atria have thinner walls
if SAN and AVN given alone for rows 1 and 2 allow 1 mark
2 delays the wave of depolarisation between the atria and the ventricles – atrioventricular node and non-conducting tissue / AW (between atria and ventricles) ;
3 transmits the wave of depolarisation through muscles of the ventricles – Purkyne / Purkinje, fibres / tissue ;
4 closes when the left ventricle contracts – left atrioventricular / bicuspid / mitral, valve ;
points.guidance: R right atrioventricular valve; I AV valves
